texto: It begins with the imperfect (context): **La prima volta a Roma avevo solo venti anni** (the first time in Rome was only twenty years old). It continues with the prossimo passage (what happened) and the trapassate (what happened above): **Ero arrivato in treno** (had arrived by train).
This is how the order of the facts is understood.

frases.it: La prima volta a Roma avevo solo venti anni.
frases.es: La primera vez que fui a Roma tenía solo veinte años.
frases.en: The first time I went to Rome, I was only 20.

frases.it: Ero arrivato in treno, ma avevo perso la strada.
frases.es: Había llegado en tren, pero me había perdido.
frases.en: I had arrived by train, but I had lost.

frases.it: Lui mi ha aiutato, e alla fine ho incontrato un amico.
frases.es: Él me ayudó, y al final encontré a un amigo.
frases.en: He helped me, and in the end I found a friend.

frases.it: Finalmente abbiamo mangiato un piatto buonissimo.
frases.es: Por fin comimos un plato riquísimo.
frases.en: We finally ate a delicious dish.

bloques.pregunta: How is «the first time» expressed in Italian?

opciones.explicacion: «Prima» (first) is gender-specific with «volta» (once).
«Strada» means street or road, no time.
It means the first time or period.

bloques.pregunta: What introduces the «alla fine» temporary locution?

opciones.explicacion: It marks the culmination of a series of events.

opciones.texto: at the beginning of the story
opciones.explicacion: The beginning would be expressed with «all\'inizio».
All of a sudden, in Italian, it's called «all\'improvviso».

bloques.frase: Il signore mi ___, e alla fine ho trovato la strada giusta.

opciones.explicacion: «aiutare» verb prossimo passport with «avere» auxiliary.
«Chiedere» means asking or asking, not helping.
«Perdere» means lose.
Descriptive imperfect of a plural physical and mood state.
That prayer would place the state in present time.

opciones.texto: We got tired of it all of a sudden in the square.
opciones.explicacion: It would indicate a timely action of prossimo passage.

bloques.pregunta: What action did the speaker take?

opciones.explicacion: «Chiedere a qualcuno» is to ask for an indication or to ask someone.

opciones.texto: I said hello to an acquaintance on the street.
opciones.explicacion: Greeting is «salutare».

opciones.texto: I waited for a gentleman in the corner.
opciones.explicacion: Wait is «aspettare».

bloques.frase: Finalmente abbiamo mangiato un piatto buonissimo
bloques.traduccion: We finally ate a delicious dish.
bloques.explicacion: Prayer with resolution warning and prossimo passage with fault.

bloques.frase: Ieri sera ero ___ in ritardo alla stazione.

opciones.explicacion: The masculine singular subject governs the deinence in -or with «essere» auxiliary.
The deinence in -a corresponds to a feminine singular subject.
The deinence in -i corresponds to the plural.

bloques.pregunta: How does the word «turista» work in Italian?

opciones.texto: It has the same shape in singular for men and women (the tourist / the tourist).
opciones.explicacion: It is a "in-ist" name that distinguishes gender through the article.

opciones.texto: It changes to «turisto» when it comes to a man.
opciones.explicacion: The «turisto» form does not exist in standard Italian.

opciones.texto: Solo puede utilizarse para referirse a mujeres.
opciones.explicacion: It applies equally to both genres.

intro: Now you're going to read a travel story. See how the times of the past alternate so that you understand what happened before and what happened after.
